scope: The standing Biblioteca Nacional de Chile and its Alameda facade, with the domed central entrance, two pavilion roofs, long side and rear elevations and three mapped light wells.
era: Present standing Biblioteca Nacional at Alameda 651, with its as-built footprint, using early author-published and federal photographic evidence for surviving facade elements.

writtenSources.use: The library gives its current Alameda entrance and street number.
Government documentation describes the cadastral block, partially executed Maltese cross, two stories with plinth and mansard and subsequent modifications.
The architect’s 1924 publication contains first-floor plans and early images. The national library marks it common cultural heritage, freely usable and reproducible.
The institutional publication describes the six free-standing center columns, three tall round-head arches and central cupola.

next: Author the Alameda front and central cupola against the original public-domain view. Use the native outer and inner rings for the remaining volumes and light wells. Reconcile the approach against the frozen elevation field.
